title: Passage between separably closed fields
statement:
Let $k\subseteq k'$ be an extension of fields [def-pc-field-extension] with $k$ and $k'$ separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed], and let $\iota:\operatorname{Spec}k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the induced morphism of spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $C$ be a scheme over $k$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] whose structure morphism $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and whose underlying topological space has Krull dimension $\dim C\le1$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (the empty scheme is allowed). Let $C_{k'}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ be the base change of $C$ along $\iota$ [def-pc-base-change], with projection $\pi:C_{k'}\to C$. Let $F$ be a torsion abelian sheaf [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] on the small etale site $C_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], with inverse image $\pi^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Assume the following hypothesis (H) (the assertion of the proposition on algebraically closed extensions, prop-weil-pbc-algebraically-closed-extension, in the precise form of Step 1 of prop-weil-pbc-proper-curve-sepclosed-invariance): for every extension $K\subseteq K'$ of algebraically closed fields [def-weil-algebraic-closure], every scheme $D$ over $K$ whose structure morphism $D\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is proper and whose underlying space has $\dim D\le1$, and every torsion abelian sheaf $G$ on $D_{\Et}$, the pullback map [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] along the projection $p:D_{K'}=D\times_{\operatorname{Spec}K}\operatorname{Spec}K'\to D$ of the base change, $p^*:H^q(D_{\Et},G)\to H^q((D_{K'})_{\Et},p^{-1}G)$, is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$. Then for every $q\ge0$ the pullback map along $\pi$ [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]

$$
 \pi^*:H^q(C_{\Et},F)\longrightarrow H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\pi^{-1}F)
$$

between the etale cohomology groups [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] is an isomorphism.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E (lemma-base-change-dim-1-separably-closed), proof (the passage from algebraically closed to separably closed fields); blueprint node: literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-proper-base-change/sk-thm-p1/lemma-weil-pbc-curve-separably-closed-passage.md, order 1148

proof.text: Characteristic zero. The fields $k\subseteq k'$ have the same characteristic. Suppose it is $0$. Then $k$ is algebraically closed: a nonconstant $g\in k[T]$ has an irreducible factor $h$, and in characteristic $0$ the derivative $h'$ is nonzero of smaller degree, so $\gcd(h,h')=1$ and $h$ is separable; by the definition of separably closed [def-pc-separably-closed] $h$, hence $g$, has a root in $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Likewise $k'$ is algebraically closed. Then the claim is (H) applied to $K=k$, $K'=k'$, $D=C$, $G=F$ (the projection $p$ of (H) is $\pi$). From now on the characteristic is a prime $p_0>0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E (lemma-base-change-dim-1-separably-closed), proof (the reduction to algebraically closed fields; in characteristic 0 the purely inseparable extensions of the proof are trivial, so the lemma is the algebraically closed case itself)

proof.text: Compatible algebraic closures. Choose an algebraic closure $\bar k'$ of $k'$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] (every field has one, Stacks Tag 09GT). Let $\bar k$ be the algebraic closure of $k$ in $\bar k'$ (via $k\subseteq k'\subseteq\bar k'$) [def-weil-relative-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-algebraic-closure-algclosed] $\bar k$ is algebraically closed and algebraic over $k$, i.e. an algebraic closure of $k$, and $\bar k\subseteq\bar k'$. All four fields are subfields of $\bar k'$, so the square of inclusions $k\subseteq k'\subseteq\bar k'$, $k\subseteq\bar k\subseteq\bar k'$ commutes; this is the diagram of the proof of Lemma 0A5E. Write $a:\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $b:\operatorname{Spec}\bar k'\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$, $c:\operatorname{Spec}\bar k'\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ for the induced morphisms; then $\iota\circ b=a\circ c$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E (lemma-base-change-dim-1-separably-closed), proof (the diagram $k\to k'\to\bar k'$, $k\to\bar k\to\bar k'$); literature/stacks-project/fields.tex Theorem Tag 09GT (existence of algebraic closures)

proof.text: Purely inseparable closures. Since $k$ is separably closed of characteristic $p_0$, [lem-pc-kbar-pure-insep] shows that its algebraic closure $\bar k$ is a purely inseparable (in particular algebraic) extension of $k$. Applied to $k'$ and its algebraic closure $\bar k'$, the same lemma shows that $\bar k'/k'$ is purely inseparable.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E (lemma-base-change-dim-1-separably-closed), proof: 'Since $k$ and $k'$ are separably closed the field extensions $\bar k/k$ and $\bar k'/k'$ are algebraic and purely inseparable'

proof.text: Universal homeomorphisms. Let $C_{\bar k}=C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$ (base change along $a$) with projection $\rho:C_{\bar k}\to C$, and $C_{\bar k'}=C_{k'}\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k'}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k'$ (base change along $b$) with projection $\sigma:C_{\bar k'}\to C_{k'}$ [def-pc-base-change]. We show that $\rho$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism], i.e. that for every morphism $t:T\to C$ the projection $T\times_CC_{\bar k}\to T$ is a homeomorphism. The square defining $T\times_CC_{\bar k}$ over $t$ and $\rho$ is cartesian, and so is the square defining $C_{\bar k}$ over $f$ and $a$; by [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] the outer rectangle is cartesian: $T\times_CC_{\bar k}$, with its projection to $T$, is a fibre product of $f\circ t:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $a$, i.e. it is the base change $T_{\bar k}$ of the $k$-scheme $T$ up to a unique isomorphism over $T$. By [lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep], applied to the purely inseparable extension $\bar k/k$ (Step 3) and the $k$-scheme $T$, the canonical morphism $T_{\bar k}\to T$ is a homeomorphism; hence so is $T\times_CC_{\bar k}\to T$. The same argument with $k'\subseteq\bar k'$, the structure morphism $C_{k'}\to\operatorname{Spec}k'$ and $b$ shows that $\sigma$ is a universal homeomorphism. (lem-pc-homeo-pure-insep is quantified over all $k$-schemes $X$; that quantifier is exactly what makes $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, and its base change $\rho$, universal homeomorphisms and not only homeomorphisms.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E (lemma-base-change-dim-1-separably-closed), proof: 'In this case the morphisms $X_{\bar k}\to X$ and $X_{\bar k'}\to X_{k'}$ are universal homeomorphisms'; literature/stacks-project/algebra.tex Lemma Tag 0BRA (lemma-p-ring-map) and Section Tag 0BR5; literature/stacks-project/morphisms.tex Definition Tag 04DD

proof.text: The vertical isomorphisms. By [prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos] (Stacks Proposition 03SI), applied to the universal homeomorphism $\rho$ of Step 4 and the abelian sheaf $F$, the pullback map [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] $\rho^*:H^q(C_{\Et},F)\to H^q((C_{\bar k})_{\Et},\rho^{-1}F)$ is an isomorphism for every $q$; applied to $\sigma$ and the sheaf $\pi^{-1}F$ on $(C_{k'})_{\Et}$, the pullback map $\sigma^*:H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},\pi^{-1}F)\to H^q((C_{\bar k'})_{\Et},\sigma^{-1}\pi^{-1}F)$ is an isomorphism for every $q$. (The isomorphism of that proposition is the map induced on cohomology by pullback along the universal homeomorphism, i.e. the pullback map $u^*$; in the Lean it is AlgebraicGeometry.Etale.cohomologyMap_bijective, about cohomologyMap.)

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E (lemma-base-change-dim-1-separably-closed), proof: 'Thus the cohomology of $\mathcal F$ may be computed on $X_{\bar k}$ and the cohomology of $\mathcal F|_{X_{k'}}$ may be computed on $X_{\bar k'}$, see Proposition 03SI'; Proposition Tag 03SI (proposition-topological-invariance)

proof.text: The hypotheses of (H) for $\bar k\subseteq\bar k'$. Let $D=C_{\bar k}$, a scheme over $\bar k$ through the projection $f_{\bar k}:D\to\operatorname{Spec}\bar k$, the base change of $f$ along $a$; it is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change]. Since $\rho:D\to C$ is a homeomorphism (Step 4, with $T=C$, $t=\mathrm{id}$) and the Krull dimension of a topological space [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] is defined through chains of irreducible closed subsets, which a homeomorphism carries bijectively to one another, $\dim D=\dim C\le1$. The sheaf $G=\rho^{-1}F$ is torsion by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-torsion]. The fields $\bar k\subseteq\bar k'$ are algebraically closed (Step 2). Hence (H), applied to $K=\bar k$, $K'=\bar k'$, $D$, $G$, gives: for the base change $D_{\bar k'}=D\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\bar k}\operatorname{Spec}\bar k'$ (along $c$) with projection $p:D_{\bar k'}\to D$, the pullback $p^*:H^q(D_{\Et},G)\to H^q((D_{\bar k'})_{\Et},p^{-1}G)$ is an isomorphism for every $q$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E (lemma-base-change-dim-1-separably-closed), proof: 'Hence we deduce the general case from the case of algebraically closed fields' (applied to $X_{\bar k}$ over $\bar k$, whose base change to $\bar k'$ is $X_{\bar k'}$)

proof.text: Identifying the two base changes to $\bar k'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting], applied to the cartesian squares defining $C_{\bar k'}$ (over $b$) and $C_{k'}$ (over $\iota$), $C_{\bar k'}$ with $\pi\circ\sigma$ and its structure morphism is a fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product] of $f$ and $\iota\circ b$; applied to the squares defining $D_{\bar k'}$ (over $c$) and $D=C_{\bar k}$ (over $a$), $D_{\bar k'}$ with $\rho\circ p$ is a fibre product of $f$ and $a\circ c$. Since $\iota\circ b=a\circ c$ (Step 2), there is a unique isomorphism $\theta:C_{\bar k'}\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{\bar k'}$ with $\rho\circ p\circ\theta=\pi\circ\sigma$ compatible with the structure morphisms to $\operatorname{Spec}\bar k'$. Put $\tau=p\circ\theta:C_{\bar k'}\to C_{\bar k}$ and $w=\rho\circ\tau=\pi\circ\sigma:C_{\bar k'}\to C$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E (lemma-base-change-dim-1-separably-closed), proof (the scheme written $X_{\bar k'}$ there is at once the base change of $X_{k'}$ and of $X_{\bar k}$ to $\bar k'$)

proof.text: The bottom arrow. The isomorphism $\theta$ is a universal homeomorphism [def-weil-universal-homeomorphism] (a base change of an isomorphism is an isomorphism, hence a homeomorphism), so $\theta^*:H^q((D_{\bar k'})_{\Et},p^{-1}G)\to H^q((C_{\bar k'})_{\Et},\theta^{-1}p^{-1}G)$ is an isomorphism by [prop-weil-pbc-universal-homeomorphism-topos]. By the composition clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], with the isomorphism $c_{p,\theta}:\theta^{-1}p^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(p\circ\theta)^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], $\tau^*=(p\circ\theta)^*=H^q(c_{p,\theta,G})\circ\theta^*\circ p^*:H^q((C_{\bar k})_{\Et},\rho^{-1}F)\to H^q((C_{\bar k'})_{\Et},\tau^{-1}\rho^{-1}F)$. Here $p^*$ is an isomorphism by Step 6, and $H^q(c_{p,\theta,G})$ is an isomorphism because $c_{p,\theta,G}$ is an isomorphism of sheaves and $H^q(-)$ of the functoriality lemma is a functor ($H^q(\varphi^{-1})\circ H^q(\varphi)=H^q(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, step 1 of that lemma). So $\tau^*$ is an isomorphism for every $q$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E (lemma-base-change-dim-1-separably-closed), proof (the lower arrow $H^q(X_{\bar k})\to H^q(X_{\bar k'})$ is the algebraically closed case); literature/stacks-project/cohomology.tex Section Tag 01F7 (functoriality of the pullback in the morphism)

proof.text:
The square commutes. By the composition clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial], with the isomorphisms $c_{\rho,\tau}:\tau^{-1}\rho^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}w^{-1}$ and $c_{\pi,\sigma}:\sigma^{-1}\pi^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}w^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], the pullback along $w=\rho\circ\tau=\pi\circ\sigma$ is computed in two ways:

$$
 w^*=H^q(c_{\rho,\tau,F})\circ\tau^*\circ\rho^*=H^q(c_{\pi,\sigma,F})\circ\sigma^*\circ\pi^*:H^q(C_{\Et},F)\to H^q((C_{\bar k'})_{\Et},w^{-1}F).
$$

This is the commutative square of the proof of Lemma 0A5E, with the canonical identifications $H^q(c_{\rho,\tau,F})$, $H^q(c_{\pi,\sigma,F})$ of the two inverse images of $F$ on $C_{\bar k'}$ written out.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A5E (lemma-base-change-dim-1-separably-closed), proof (the comparison of the two routes $X_{\bar k'}\to X$); literature/stacks-project/cohomology.tex Section Tag 01F7

proof.text: Two out of three. By Step 9, $\sigma^*\circ\pi^*=H^q(c_{\pi,\sigma,F})^{-1}\circ H^q(c_{\rho,\tau,F})\circ\tau^*\circ\rho^*$, a composite of isomorphisms (Steps 5, 8, and Step 8's remark that $H^q$ of an isomorphism of sheaves is an isomorphism). Since $\sigma^*$ is an isomorphism (Step 5), $\pi^*=(\sigma^*)^{-1}\circ(\sigma^*\circ\pi^*)$ is an isomorphism for every $q\ge0$.
